title: UFO — One game, three muted locations

shared_rules.geometry: Rounded, simple low-poly animals; comic humans; restrained reusable environment geometry.
shared_rules.player: The same cobalt/petrol-blue saucer with matching dome, three mint lights and crooked antenna.
shared_rules.targets: Warm ivory/black cattle, cream sheep, salmon pigs; warm skin, amber headwear and navy clothes. Local wardrobe changes preserve the same character family.
shared_rules.environment: Only low-saturation shades of one location-specific hue for all scenery, including roofs, trees, paths and props.
shared_rules.effects: Mint capture circles/trails and laser; coral military warnings and projectiles; dark charcoal-blue enemy vehicles.
shared_rules.interface: Matching compact navy top HUD; no permanent bottom upgrade tray during ordinary play.
shared_rules.composition: Matched overhead camera, framing and actor placement make the three location palettes directly comparable.

frames.name: sage-farmland
frames.title: Sage Farmland
frames.description: Open paddocks, low barn roofs and crop-circle traces; the whole environment shares a muted sage-grey family.
frames.style: LOCATION 1 OF 3 — SAGE FARMLAND. The ENTIRE static environment uses low-saturation SAGE-GREY tones, like a quiet monochrome miniature: medium sage ground, slightly lighter sage dirt paths, darker sage roof planes and simplified sage tree crowns, matching sage fences and hay cylinders. Hue family roughly #71857A, #8C9C90, #526A60, #AAB6AA, kept muted. No purple trees, red barns, golden hay or colourful flowers. Distinct farm geography: open paddocks, one small barn roof clipped on left, sparse crop rows and a faint old crop-circle impression well away from active radius. Rounded low-poly trees and fences frame boundaries, lots of unbroken quiet central ground. Full-colour ivory cattle, cream sheep, salmon pigs, navy/amber farmers stand out as the obvious abductable targets. Include one lanky farmer and one pear-shaped cow in funny capture poses. The reference's abduction comedy and softness survive; colour separation resembles reference image 4, but environment is sage-grey instead of slate. Same ivory/petrol UFO and mint effects. Clean practical top-down gameplay composition. This first image establishes the master models, camera, renderer, scale, HUD and target palette for the remaining two locations.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: one 9:16 portrait gameplay style frame for ONE coherent mobile UFO-abduction endless-runner game with several locations, not a different game per location.
Reference roles: image 1 provides the rounded cow forms, crop-circle humour and quiet playable ground; image 2 provides the sleepy domestic humour and neighbourhood possibility; image 3 provides lanky elastic human limbs, big hats, floating hat gag and tapered funny cow silhouette; image 4 provides the CRUCIAL near-monochrome scenery / full-colour collectible separation. Synthesize these references into a single coherent polished shippable LOW-POLY 3D art style. Do not reproduce four different renderers.

LOCKED GAME ART: same small ivory saucer with deep PETROL-BLUE hemispherical dome, three mint lamps and tiny crooked antenna in every location; UFO around 10–12 percent of width, lower-middle screen, no face or arms. The same cows: comically pear-shaped warm IVORY bodies, BLACK patches, tiny coral nose, huge black paddle ears and thin small legs. Same cream scalloped sheep, salmon-pink bean pigs. Same human mesh family: small warm peach head, lanky navy-overall body, long flexible arms, oversized AMBER hat, big dark bean boots. Wardrobe can vary locally without changing proportions or renderer. Abducted human flails, loose amber hat spirals separately, small cow tips belly-up. Keep warmth, personality and funny low-poly shapes rather than realistic simulation.

STRICT COLOUR HIERARCHY: 80–85 percent of image consists of QUIET nearly MONOCHROMATIC scenery in the chosen environment hue. ALL non-collectible static props, roofs, walls, trees, paths, fences, road markings and shrubs belong to desaturated shades of that SAME hue. No colourful roofs, plants, hay, cars, yellow windows or signs competing with collectibles. The full-colour warm amber/ivory/salmon HUMAN AND ANIMAL TARGETS stand out sharply in both value and saturation. Do not apply an overall colour tint to the living targets; keep their albedo identical across locations. Military vehicles use the same dark charcoal-blue material in all three, with compact CORAL chevron warnings and tiny coral projectiles, clearly separate from the warm organic targets. UFO and live effects use IVORY / PETROL / MINT, unchanged between scenes. World material is consistent matte flat-shaded low-poly with light tactile softness, short soft shadows, no elaborate textures, outlines, photo grain, bloom or depth of field. Simple scene meshes and one clear lighting setup.

PLAYABLE COMPOSITION: overhead top-down game camera, same high angle and zoom as references, ground fills frame, no sky or horizon, no side-view panorama. Small scattered targets and threats at actual game scale, wide open travel space ahead, reusable edge scenery. Saucer travel is upward. Thin MINT ground-plane capture radius and exactly TWO SHORT curved dotted capture trails to small human/cow, no tractor-beam cone. One slim mint laser intercepts ONE coral missile with a tiny spark, no explosion or giant smoke trail. Tank at upper edge, jeep at side. Plenty of uncollected people/animals ahead. No target brackets or dense science annotations. Same HUD in all three: a slim dark PETROL top strip, ivory score "12,480", "LV 07", mint XP progress meter and three ivory shield pips; no bottom upgrade cards in this ordinary gameplay state. No title, location label, watermark, phone mockup or other captions. Full bleed art, all gameplay elements in focus.

frames.name: slate-suburbia
frames.title: Slate Suburbia
frames.description: Sleepy residential streets and front gardens, all rendered in subdued slate-blue while the shared warm target palette remains intact.
frames.style:
Use case: stylized-concept. Generate ONE new 9:16 portrait mobile gameplay frame.
REFERENCE ROLES: Image 1 (sage farmland) is the MASTER FOR THIS SAME GAME: exactly match its camera, zoom, low-poly renderer, round pear-shaped cow model, funny human proportions, sheep/pig meshes, blue UFO, mint capture effects, enemy models and HUD layout. Image 2 (old sleepy suburbia) is ONLY a location/wardrobe reference for residential street shapes and sleepy domestic comedy. Ignore the different UFO, lighting colours, model proportions and interface of image 2. This is the SAME GAME as image 1, with environment meshes and their monochrome hue changed.

LOCATION 2 — SLATE SUBURBIA. A sleepy suburban street with gently curved kerbs and small roof-only detached houses clipped along both edges, small simple front gardens and letterboxes. One generous street junction in the upper third, broad empty road area ahead of the saucer, no farms, crop rows, hay, barn or crop-circle marking on the road. Near-monochrome environment exclusively in low-saturation SLATE BLUE / BLUE-GREY tones, roughly #66788C, #8292A3, #4D6075, #A4AFBA. ALL static scenery stays blue-grey: roofs are blue-grey, walls blue-grey, street blue-grey, pavements lighter blue-grey, bushes darker blue-grey, door/window planes grey-blue with subtle neutral light. Absolutely NO red roofs, green lawns, yellow windows, orange streetlights or bright mailboxes. Preserve readable soft neutral illumination rather than tinting the cast blue. Do not make this extremely dark.

Full-colour living targets POP exactly like in master: cream/black pear-cows with coral noses, cream sheep, salmon pig, tiny warm-skinned comic people with amber/yellow headwear, navy/cream clothing and big bean boots. Local human wardrobe includes oversized amber nightcaps and flared navy/cream bathrobes on the SAME small character rig/proportions; one familiar straw-hatted navy farmer can also be present. One bathrobe character flails with an amber nightcap floating away and one master-model cow turns belly-up in capture. The SAME deep blue saucer and mint lights remain lower-middle, same short mint curved capture trails/circle and same slim laser/coral enemy markings. Match the master top HUD exactly: three small dark navy groups, ivory "12,480", "LV 07" plus mint XP, three mint/ivory shield pips. No bottom cards, no title/location label. The visual read should be 'identical game, different biome' with immediate muted-world versus warm-living-target separation. Buildable mobile low-poly style; don't increase detail just because this is a town.

frames.name: mauve-desert-roadside
frames.title: Mauve Desert Roadside
frames.description: Broad desert ground, angular rock outcrops, cacti and a roadside canopy in muted mauve; the same coloured cast and effects maintain the game's identity.
frames.style:
Use case: stylized-concept. Generate ONE 9:16 portrait gameplay style frame for location 3 of this EXACT SAME GAME.
REFERENCE ROLES: Images 1 and 2 are the approved unified game's master look in two locations. Copy the same high overhead camera angle, zoom, renderer, model detail, target colour palette, UFO shape, enemy models, mint capture effects and top HUD. This is a new desert location using the same asset family, NOT a new art style or redesign.

LOCATION 3 — MAUVE DESERT ROADSIDE. The whole non-interactive world is rendered in ONE muted DUSTY MAUVE / WARM PLUM-GREY colour family: medium grey-mauve sandy ground, slightly lighter mauve tracks, darker muted plum rock outcrops, faceted mauve cactus silhouettes, a tiny roof-only roadside service canopy clipped at one edge, its supports and nearby posts matching mauve. Rough palette #8C7785, #AA95A1, #6C5868, #B8A4AD. No orange/yellow sand, green cacti, red roofs, neon signs, blue structures, or multicoloured scenery. Shade variation within the ONE muted hue provides terrain legibility. Geometry should clearly describe a dry wide roadside desert with chunky rock formations and spaced cacti, NOT a recoloured farm or suburban street. No barn, fences, crop rows, circular trees or hay. One broad pale-mauve road curves along the LEFT edge, rock shelves and cacti crop along right and top edges, centre is a quiet open dirt route. Only a few broad flat stones, no detailed sand or decorative clutter. Shift the small edge layouts and target positions to make this genuinely a third place, while keeping camera, scale and player position stable.

PRESERVE EXACT SHARED GAME CAST: the small deep BLUE saucer with blue dome, three mint lights and crooked antenna from reference 1, lower-middle at same scale. Same full-colour warm IVORY pear-shaped black-spotted cows, same cream scalloped sheep, salmon bean pigs, same tiny warm-skinned lanky navy farmers with big AMBER hats and dark boots. Civilian costume can have a simple oversized local sunhat but keep the same rig and colours. Do not tint actors mauve. It should be instantly obvious that every full-colour human/animal is abductable against the muted environment. One upside-down cow and one flailing human with hat floating away follow two short mint dotted capture paths into the SAME saucer; same circular mint ground footprint. Same tiny dark charcoal-blue tank at top and jeep at left with coral chevron warnings, single coral missile and one narrow mint laser/tiny spark. Military material and coral signals do not change by biome.

COHERENT ART: simple matte low-poly models, broad rounded shapes plus slight elastic humour, short soft shadows and soft neutral light identical to references. No pixel art, voxel blocks, outline comic style, craft materials, photographic detail, camera tilt changes or horizon. Same compact top HUD layout and colours: dark-navy rounded groups, ivory score "12,480", "LV 07", mint XP meter, three mint shield pips. No bottom cards, no location name, no captions, branding, watermark or phone frame. Full bleed mobile screenshot with plenty of open travel space and small readable play objects. The final result should look like three environments in one art-directed real mobile game, using near-monochrome scenery to spotlight the same colourful abduction targets.
